correctness.rationale: The finite-population coupling is reconstructed explicitly for each geometry: same row H(N-b,d,a-x), same column H(N-a,c,b-x), distinct rows/columns K=H(N-b,d,a-x) followed by Y=H(N-a,d-K,c). Both nested-sample and nested-marked-set couplings give stochastic order across all attainable x, including endpoints. The symmetrized independent-copy identity gives covariance for all nondecreasing transforms, and the indicator expansion gives the exact covariance formulas. Independent exhaustive permutation enumeration for 151 margin pairs with N<=6 confirms 48,818 exact rational inequalities and identities. It is finite corroboration, not a proof of all N.

originality.rationale: The Fisher–Yates law, hypergeometric marginals, and asymptotic covariance structure are prior work, explicitly credited. The surviving claim is a finite-N conditional first-order stochastic ordering for *every* pair of cell positions and all increasing transforms; it goes beyond covariance and answers the pairwise aspect of the zero-position dependence question in Paguyo (2021). Relevant full-text sections of three closely related primary papers do not assert this ordering. General sampling-without-replacement literature can imply special cases; residual implicit-equivalence risk remains, and this is not an independent historical priority determination.
residual_risks: A classical multivariate hypergeometric/urn negative-regression theorem may imply this full pairwise classification indirectly; historical priority has not been independently established.
Joe (1985) and older exact-conditional contingency-table literature were not available as complete full text; accessible records concern table majorization rather than conditional cell order.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete finite-sample spatial-dependence classification for every pair of fixed-margin table cells, including zero-location events singled out as a question in Paguyo (2021). In contrast to the familiar covariance matrix, it uniformly controls every threshold probability and every increasing transform at arbitrary heterogeneous positive margins, and explains a checkerboard sign geometry (e.g. positive 23/450 across disjoint cells and negative -7/75 along a row for 3x3 margins 2). The exact pairwise classification is a motivated structural invariant, not an arbitrary parameter slice or marginal recount.
